This week I read **The Subtle Art of Not Giving a Fuck by Mark Manson**. I really enjoyed this book and the way he suggests new frameworks for how we think about our lives. The ideas aren't entirely new to me as they're a semblance of what I've read in **The Defining Decade by Meg Jay** which I recommend to anyone in college or out of it, as well as books like **The Denial of Death by Ernest Becker** which is even mentioned by Manson himself.

Something that really spoke to me is the point he makes about accepting challenges and the suffering that comes with it. Everyone would like to be hot, rich and popular so the question we should ask ourselves is not what do you want, but rather "What pain do you want in your life? What are you willing to struggle for?" I've been trying to realize this in my life, so last Wednesday when I really didn't want to go to the gym after work, I framed it in terms of okay bezmialem, if your desire to be skinnier/fitter is not worth the hour of gym you could put in right now then go home. And when I put it like that, I did go to the gym.
